decision: per-line content hashes + a window scan, no AST.
why: Add tree-sitter when a real repo produces orphans this cannot explain.

A 3k-line file against a 10-line span is ~30k hash comparisons — microseconds, and it only runs on records that already failed both cheap checks. Revisit if capture ever starts anchoring records to spans hundreds of lines long.

decision: comment syntax by prefix, not by parser.
why: Covers //, # and block- comment continuations, which is every language in this repo. A note inside a language that comments some other way is simply not harvested — silent, but silent-and-absent rather than silent-and-wrong.

decision: whole-file JSON read and a linear scan in Match.
why: Fine at the ~20 hand-written records of Phase 0 (microseconds). Move to SQLite with an index on (file, line_start, line_end) once Phase 1 capture makes this thousands of records, because PreToolUse blocks every edit and latency becomes visible.

decision: PreToolUse lookup measured at 6.3ms per fire, so no caching or daemon.
why: Measured 2026-08-01: 100 hook invocations in 0.629s wall, against the plan's 300ms-per-edit risk and a 5s timeout. The time split (0.24s user, 0.35s system) puts most of it in fork/exec, not in the file read or the window scan — so a persistent process would win back almost nothing, and the SQLite migration at record.go:82 is not latency-driven.

decision: 6 hex chars, ~16.7M values, so collisions get likely somewhere around a few thousand records.
why: Records already written keep their 4-char ids; nothing parses an id's length. Widen again, or key on a real hash, if the store ever gets that big.

Real relevance ranking (does this record concern the lines actually being changed?) needs a diff. `why check` now exists and has one — but this is PreToolUse, which fires *before* the edit, so there is no diff here to rank against and there cannot be. The trigger this note used to carry ("revisit when check exists") was the wrong trigger. The right one is a hook that runs after an edit: PostToolUse could rank by what actually changed, at the cost of arriving too late to stop anything.

decision: this counts SURFACINGS, not caught contradictions, so it over-counts — most surfacings are purely informational.
why: Do not read this file as the DECISIONS §8 falsification metric. That number now comes from `why check`, which compares a diff against records; count the records it reports and how many turned out to matter.

decision: Rotted grounds are announced, not silently dropped.
why: A record whose evidence has been deleted still reads as authoritative — the decision text is unchanged and its own anchor may be perfectly exact. Without saying GONE here, a reader cannot tell a grounded record from one that merely looks grounded, which is the failure DECISIONS §17 is about.
